profile.niche: Home workouts for busy office workers who want to get fit but can't make it to a gym
profile.audience: Home workouts for busy office workers who want to get fit but can't make it to a gym

research_material:
i sit at a desk for 8 hours straight and by the time i get home i just want to collapse. how do people actually find energy to work out after that?
my apartment is tiny so i can't do anything that needs space or equipment. just looking for stuff i can do in like 20 mins between calls
tried going to the gym for 2 weeks and the membership was so expensive plus the commute killed me. has to be something i can do at home before work
my back is always sore from my chair and i feel like i'm getting softer every year but i genuinely don't have time to drive anywhere. what actually works
been telling myself i'll work out for months but by 6pm my brain is fried. need something simple that doesn't require me to think too hard about it

pain_points: Mental and physical exhaustion after 8 hours of desk work makes motivation nearly impossible
Lack of space and equipment at home limits workout options
Time constraints require workouts to fit into tiny windows (20 mins, before work)
Chronic back pain and postural issues from sitting all day
Decision fatigue and lack of mental energy to plan or think through workouts

missing_info: What time do these office workers wake up? (crucial for pre-work content feasibility)
Do they have ANY equipment at home (resistance bands, dumbbells) or is it truly bodyweight only?
What does 'back pain' look like for them? (Lower back, upper back, all-day soreness?) — affects exercise focus
Have any of them tried working out before and quit? Why specifically did they stop?
Are there any 'success stories' in the audience (office workers who ARE finding time to work out at home)? What are they doing differently?

hooks.text: Your brain's too tired to pick a workout. Here's the fix.
What if your workout required zero decisions?
Press play. Follow along. Done in 20 minutes.
The fitness industry's been doing this backwards the whole time.
Decision fatigue is why you skip workouts. Not laziness.
This is the workout format gym bros won't tell you about.
No planning. No options. Just results.
Most home workout fails happen before you even start moving.
One question: why are you still thinking during workouts?
The secret isn't harder work. It's fewer choices.

winner.text: Press play. Follow along. Done in 20 minutes.
winner.reasoning: This hook speaks directly to the time-constrained office worker by making the entire process frictionless—no research, no decisions, immediate action. For busy professionals drowning in choices all day, the simplicity itself becomes the primary benefit and removes the cognitive barrier that prevents workouts from happening.

runner_up.text: Decision fatigue is why you skip workouts. Not laziness.
runner_up.reasoning: This hook names the specific pain point that resonates with office workers while reframing their struggle as a legitimate problem (not personal failure). It validates their experience and makes them feel understood before introducing the solution.

script.script:
HOOK [0-3 sec]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: 20-MINUTE WORKOUT]
Press play. [excited] Follow along. Done in 20 minutes.

[CUT]

PROBLEM
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: NO GYM. NO TIME. NO EXCUSES.]
You're sitting at a desk eight hours a day. [sighs] By the time you get home, the gym feels impossible.

[PAUSE]

VALUE
But here's the thing: you don't need a gym. [serious] This workout hits every major muscle group with zero equipment. Just your body weight. Just 20 minutes. Just your living room.

[CUT]

[ON-SCREEN TEXT: FULL BODY. NO EXCUSES.]
Squats. Push-ups. Burpees. [curious] Simple moves. Real results.

Do this three times a week and you'll feel the difference in two weeks. [direct] No fluff. No commute. No membership.

[PAUSE]

CTA
Follow for more workouts that actually fit your life.

[ON-SCREEN TEXT: @[HANDLE] FOR MORE]
script.viewer_takeaway: A fit, strong body is possible even with a packed schedule—all you need is 20 minutes, no equipment, and the willingness to start today.

cover_options: Confident person mid-burpee in a bright living room, sweat visible, direct eye contact with camera, bold text overlay: '20-MINUTE WORKOUT'
Split-screen: left side shows person at desk looking tired, right side shows same person energized doing a push-up at home, text: 'NO GYM. NO TIME. NO EXCUSES.'

frame_plan.visual_direction: Close-up of person's face, energized expression, looking directly at camera. Quick cut to them in workout clothes in living room. Fast, punchy energy.
B-roll: person pressing play on phone/tablet, sitting down at desk, then sighing/looking tired. Show the problem visually.
Medium shot of person at desk (8+ hour setup visible—computer, chair). Tired expression, slow movements. Transition to them getting home, looking exhausted on couch.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: NO GYM. NO TIME. NO EXCUSES.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Person in living room, serious/confident expression. Quick demo cuts: squat (full body visible), push-up (face visible from side angle), burpee (dynamic, face visible). Show smooth form.
Person wiping sweat, catching breath, smiling directly at camera. Show confidence/accomplishment. Living room setting reinforces 'no gym' message.
Person gives direct nod/wink to camera, or gives thumbs up. End on their confident face. Text appears in bottom third.

assets_needed: Bright, clean living room as primary location
Office desk setup (optional, can be minimal)

justifications.clarity: Hook lands immediately with '20-minute workout' and value prop is stated by 5 seconds; problem-solution structure is direct.
justifications.retention: Problem-agitate-solve keeps viewer engaged, but middle section (exercise names) lacks emotional payoff or visual surprise to prevent thumb-scroll.
justifications.save_potential: Tight script, strong visuals planned, and clear use case make this worth keeping in rotation; addresses real objection (time/access).
justifications.shareability: Relatable pain point (desk job exhaustion) has viral potential, but lacks novelty angle or specific transformation hook that drives shares.
justifications.audience_fit: Perfectly mirrors target audience's constraints (no gym, no time, home-based); desk setup and living room setting reinforce relevance.
justifications.cta_strength: Follow-for-more is safe but generic; doesn't create urgency or specific incentive (e.g., 'free 20-min routine,' 'daily workouts,' 'no equipment needed').

weaknesses.issue: CTA is passive ('follow for more workouts') with no urgency or specific value beyond what's already shown—viewer has no reason to follow *now* instead of later.
weaknesses.fix: Replace 'Follow for more workouts that actually fit your life' with 'Follow for a new 20-minute routine every Monday—no equipment, no excuses' or 'Follow to get the full routine + daily challenges in our stories.'

weaknesses.issue: Middle section lists exercises (squats, push-ups, burpees) without showing transformation or emotional reward—just mechanics—which kills retention momentum after hook.
weaknesses.fix: Replace 'Squats. Push-ups. Burpees. Simple moves. Real results. Do this three times a week and you'll feel the difference in two weeks.' with 'Five simple moves. Three times a week. After two weeks: stronger, less tired at your desk, actually want to move. That's the difference.'

weaknesses.issue: No hook variant addresses the 'shareability gap'—people won't share a generic time-saver; they share identity or status—this reads as self-help, not flex.
weaknesses.fix: Reframe hook from 'Press play. Follow along. Done in 20 minutes' to 'Built a 20-minute routine that beats a 90-minute gym session—from your living room' or 'Desk job for 8 hours. Gym? Nope. Still stronger than most.' to add aspiration/identity.

captions: 20 minutes. Your living room. Zero excuses. No gym membership, no commute, no time wasted—just real results from home. Hit every muscle group with moves you can do in your work clothes (before the shower). Save this and do it 3x this week. Follow for workouts that actually fit your life.

8 hours at a desk = zero energy for the gym. But 20 minutes at home? That you can do. Squats, push-ups, burpees—full body, no equipment, no fluff. Do this three times a week and watch your energy (and strength) shift in two weeks. Follow for a new routine every Monday.
growth.final_call_reason: Strong audience fit and structure, but CTA lacks urgency and middle section doesn't create emotional retention—rewrite to add transformation language and specific follow incentive before posting.
